title: the bridge at baghdad
label: the imam who spent nineteen years in custody
caption:
Al-Sindi b. Shahik ran the prison where Musa b. Ja'far died. He did not
bury the body. He walked the jurists of Baghdad past it, had them state
that they saw no wound, then carried it to the bridge and invited the
city to look at the face.

A man does not stage a viewing to prove a death nobody doubts.

Sources are named on the slides. Every figure traces to a page in the
edition cited, and where the chronicles differ the slides say so.

title: thirty-seven names
label: the arithmetic of a succession
caption:
Al-Mufid lists the children of Musa b. Ja'far by name: thirty-seven, sons
and daughters, with the mothers marked. A household that size is not a
family detail. It is the size of the problem the succession had to solve.

title: no mark upon him
label: the jurists who were asked to look
caption:
Al-Sindi b. Shahik did not ask the jurists of Baghdad whether the prisoner
had been poisoned. He asked them whether they could see a wound. They
could not, and they said so, and he wrote it down. The question you are
asked decides the answer you can give.
